title: Raking Between Bunker Shots
question: If your ball stays in the same bunker after your first shot, can you rake away footprints or disturbed sand from your previous shot before you play your next stroke?

choices.text: Yes, and you can ground your club behind the ball too
No, you aren’t allowed to touch the sand at all
Yes, but you still can't ground your club behind the ball or during a practice swing
No, you must leave the sand as it is and play your next shot

explanation: You may rake the sand to care for the course, but you still can't ground your club behind the ball or touch the sand during your stance or a practice swing.
imagePrompt: A teen girl rakes her footprints away in a bunker while her ball remains further ahead in the sand.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer raking sand in a bunker, preparing for a second shot with the ball still inside the bunker.

issues: Wedge appears to be lying on the bunker sand rather than actively held, but this is acceptable for the context of raking.
Left-handedness of the golfer is not entirely clear from pose; could be made more obvious, but not a significant realism issue.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the golf wedge is held in the teen girl's other hand, clearly showing a left-handed grip, while she uses the rake to smooth the sand. Make the left-handed posture more distinct.
